title: thebasics:thebasics-handbook-title-scene-markers
text: Scene markers hold persistent roleplay descriptions without filling a build with large written signs. Craft one from any two loose stones, then place the small marker flat on the ground or against a wall. Writing and reading - Hold Shift and right-click a placed marker to edit its optional title, body, and presentation. - Choose Environmental description for in-fiction narration, or OOC notice for explicit production notes. - Look directly at a written marker to see its description over the world. Choose Stone to keep the marker unobtrusive, or a symbol to invite nearby players to inspect it. - Break a marker to pick it up with its title, description, presentation, and author metadata intact. Hold Shift and right-click the item to read it. Editing follows normal land-claim permissions. Scene markers are durable world content, separate from temporary /envhere and !! cast messages and separate from local or global OOC chat settings. Padlocks The creator can sneak-right-click with a padlock to lock a marker, without reinforcing it first. Everyone can still read it. While locked, editing is disabled; only its creator or a server admin with claim access can break or unlock it. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to unlock and recover the padlock. Picking up and replacing a locked marker preserves its lock and creator. Editing never transfers ownership. Normal land-claim permissions still apply. Appearance Use the editor tiles and preview to choose Stone, a modeled 3D symbol, a camera-facing Billboard, or Hybrid (base plus billboard). Choose an exclamation, question, or information symbol. Billboard distance accepts 1-1024 blocks (default 24): the icon fades through the outer quarter of that distance. Unlimited removes the distance fade but still requires loaded terrain. Walls obscure the billboard. Physical models and bases do not distance-fade. Appearance and distance settings survive pickup and replacement, and locked markers must be unlocked before changing them.
